baer-heitev/7:א: From half of it. Taz, Bach, and Chavot Yair siman 227.
beer-hagolah/2:ב: Tosafot there, and likewise the Tur.
beer-hagolah/6:א: Tur in the name of Maharam of Rothenburg.
beer-hagolah/7:ג: Tur in the name of Avi HaEzri and Hagahot Mordechai in the name of R' Yakir.
beur-hagra/6:ד: And even if he took it. Therefore no question it diminishes, as written in Eruvin 2a alleyways of rabbinic origin, etc., because diminution implies while still burning, etc. — see there: the kindling, etc. So Beit Yosef copied in the name of Tosafot, but it is not in our Tosafot; however apparently so from what Tosafot wrote 22a s.v. Hanukkah light. As proven below; meaning as written 23a lamp, etc. — see Tosafot there d.h. mechabeh, etc.; but at the beginning of Sukkah s.v. d'oraisa wrote even per that view, etc.; therefore they aimed likewise in Tosafot Shabbat, and some say for lamp, etc., that they challenged — and you would say, etc. — there it rests in its place.
beur-hagra/7:ג: And nevertheless the custom, etc. So too Maharil and Terumat HaDeshen and Mordechai and Tur — except no proof from Mordechai and Tur, for in their days they kindled at the house entrance as Tur wrote end siman 672. R' Moshe. And this is what he wrote "if so," etc., as below seif 2.
beur-hagra/7:ה: On the southern wall. In memory of the menorah, and also because of arrangement as in Hagahah and he arranges them, etc. Terumat HaDeshen wrote because we hold halacha follows Rabbi over his colleague, and so Rashi holds as in end of chapter 2 Shabbat and in explanation of Torah; but Rambam ruled like his colleague in his code and like R' Eliezer ben Shamua in Menorah, and so Semag; their reason: we hold like Rabbi over his colleague, and anonymous Mishnah in Menachot there is like Rabbi as Tosafot there 96a d.h. kol, 98b d.h. mizrach, etc.; so Rambam there like the Mishnah, and Rambam copied there halacha 8; but in Menorah he ruled like Ra'avad because sugya Megillah 21b follows him. However Ra'avad there attacked him and wrote the Mishnah of Tamid is like Rabbi; so Tosafot Menachot 98b d.h. midkhtiv, etc.; Rambam in commentary there wrote we do not hold like that Mishnah.
biur-halacha/4:ג: Even with Shabbat lights, etc. — from the wording it implies even on Shabbat and Yom Tov one must be careful not to do so — it is not so, for on Shabbat and Yom Tov mitzvah to make bundles as above siman 663; Magen Avraham already questioned thus; see end of his words: according to what he concludes in the name of Maharshal, forbidden in our context even two bundled lights — automatically no explanation for Rama's words concluding even Shabbat and Yom Tov lights one must be careful; see Peri Megadim who also strained greatly on Rama's words; in my humble opinion it appears one detail is missing mentioned in Or Zarua: when they glue them after kindling until they heat and fall — this is truly forbidden whether Hanukkah or Shabbat and Yom Tov: "Darkei Moshe: when kindling Shabbat or Hanukkah or Yom Tov light and glue candles near each other until they heat one another and wax drips and doubles and falls — they did not fulfill the mitzvah" — Or Zarua — end; for truth is as Rama cited Or Zarua; the first law is not mentioned in Or Zarua, only this law.
biur-halacha/5:ב: And one needs another light to use for its illumination — Rashi explains because of recognition; meaning even if he does not want at all to use its light, nevertheless he needs another light so he has ability to use its light, and thereby it is recognizable the first is for mitzvah — otherwise since it stands on the table they will say he kindled for his need. It appears specifically when placing on his table; but all who place near the entrance do not need another light even though it stands for him, since he does not come to use its light for any use. However world custom and our rabbis' custom: for all Hanukkah lights kindled inside the house, another light is required even if no use needed, lest they say he kindled for his need; so I practice — so Meiri — see there; see Peri Megadim that responsa of Rama also implies thus; see end siman 678 s.k. 3 Magen Avraham: even one who has only one light [and no other to kindle to use its light] — nevertheless he kindles and blesses on it; nevertheless l'chatchila certainly be careful not to use beforehand.
chokhmat-shlomo/2:_: (Same, seif 6) But if he places it above twenty amot he has not fulfilled, etc. NB: See Tur and Taz dispute whether walls reaching ceiling helps — R' Yehuda HaLevi holds it helps, Tur disputes — see there. In my humble opinion proof for Tur from Gemara language source of this law chapter 2 Shabbat: Hanukkah light placed above twenty amot is invalid like sukkah and like alley — one should deduce on this lengthy wording: it should say briefly invalid, and one of sukkah or like alley alone suffices — why both like sukkah and like alley? Intent: we hold like Rava sukkah reason from temporary dwelling required; therefore invalid even if walls reach sechach as we hold Shulchan Aruch siman 633; therefore R' Tanchum from whom this law is sourced holds like Rava: in sukkah invalid in every respect even if walls reach sechach — therefore had to cite both: if only like alley, one might think since reason eye does not dominate, if walls reach ceiling valid even for Hanukkah — therefore teaches invalid like sukkah: as in sukkah invalid even walls reach sechach, so here invalid even walls reach ceiling. If only sukkah cited, we would not know invalid reason — in sukkah if walls reach sechach eye dominates, only invalid from other reason temporary dwelling required — then in Hanukkah that reason does not apply, why invalid if walls reach ceiling? Therefore said like alley where reason eye does not dominate — teaches well invalid in sukkah even walls reach ceiling. Alley reason: eye does not dominate — even walls reach ceiling applies — Tur's words and great support for Tur's view — examine. I was uncertain: if he placed the light partly below twenty and partly above twenty, as wax candle — fulfilled or not? In sukkah siman 633 and alley siman 363 seif 26 we hold valid, as Gemara concludes Eruvin 3b: hollow sukkah we learned, hollow alley we learned — here what? It appears to resolve from Gemara language: Hanukkah light placed above twenty amot invalid like sukkah and like alley — why this length — suffice "placed above twenty invalid," and silence implies like sukkah and alley hollow sukkah and hollow alley; if we deepen: should cite only one invalid like sukkah or invalid like alley; one could say sukkah cited to exclude Ra'avyah Tur brought who holds walls reaching ceiling valid for Hanukkah above twenty — Tur disputes; therefore for us who hold sukkah invalid from permanent dwelling — sukkah invalid even walls reach sechach siman 633 — teaches invalid like sukkah even reaching ceiling; what cites alley: as we hold above siman 633 sechach above twenty and projections descend within twenty — if subtract above, shadow majority valid, else invalid; Taz there brought Ran: partial sechach above twenty and partial within twenty valid — implies even without majority shadow within twenty only projections reduce — see there; in my humble opinion not so — only in sukkah we require majority shadow; what Gemara did not explain — relied on explicit sugya regarding projections; in crossbeam appears well: did not distinguish whether that part could stand alone or not — therefore no support here — appears permits even if could not stand alone if top removed; reason: crossbeam since essentially sufficient by majority because of recognition, only it would fall — what difference whether standing by something; now not falling, main validation here it is below and becomes like iron spit; but in sechach main validation only by combination above — if not enough below, does not help — such is reasoning. Therefore in Hanukkah if part of light within twenty and part above twenty, even if below not enough alone, with combination above valid like alley not like sukkah — therefore cited sukkah for walls reaching ceiling not helping, and alley for part within twenty part above; further distinction alley versus sukkah: sukkah temporary dwelling — what if part within twenty, eventually top above is invalid, no combination; crossbeam recognition — if part within twenty and sees by it, sight governs also above — therefore above also valid — very sound. Therefore Hanukkah too recognition — valid if part within twenty part above — this too is alley; cited sukkah walls reaching ceiling not helping even recognition — Tur's view; cited sukkah for us walls reaching sechach not helping; cited alley part within part above. While engaged I greatly wonder at poskim who copied this Gemara language "Hanukkah light placed above twenty invalid" — wondrous, for in Eruvin Gemara concludes hollow sukkah we learned hollow alley we learned — if sechach above twenty and crossbeam likewise valid if hollow only twenty — there they cited body of sukkah and alley themselves above twenty — then invalid when crossbeam and sechach above twenty amot; but here Hanukkah they cited law on body of light placed above twenty invalid — why? behold if hollow only twenty valid as sukkah and alley, and there too valid thus; one who says so would think sukkah and alley invalid even if hollow only twenty; but for us who hold valid — should not cite this language, only "if hollow under light above twenty invalid." Perhaps since in Hanukkah main publicity is light — if crossbeam and sechach from bottom to sechach reaches twenty valid; but Hanukkah since light has some length and main publicity is light — all body above twenty, light is above above twenty — as if hollow body more than twenty — examine, still requires study.
machatzit-hashekel/7:_: (S.k. 7) The kindling, etc. — he cited it as proven below siman 675 seif 1: if kindled inside and took outside — not fulfilled from that reason; but for law I do not know practical difference between reason Shulchan Aruch gave kindling l'shem mitzvah and requires kindling in its place, and Maharshal's reason they will say for his need, etc., and if he kindled below twenty and removed from there and placed elsewhere within twenty — for both reasons he fulfills, for both places are valid called "place," and no need in such case for his need, etc., as Magen Avraham wrote above siman 663 s.k. 23 — see there; see below siman 675 Magen Avraham s.k. 3.
mishnah-berurah/6:ב: (27) Below nineteen — there is more pirsumei nisa when below, for something made for light is not normally placed so low; see Eliyah Rabbah who wrote world is not careful because they rely on Mordechai who wrote nowadays accustomed inside, no stringency; however Tur ruled anonymously implying he holds no distinction; so all careful practice as Beit Yosef wrote. If he lives in upper story he places in window toward public domain even if window higher than nineteen from upper floor ground. If two windows, one above nineteen one below — certainly place below nineteen. Synagogue lights — custom menorah in high place.
mishnah-berurah/7:נ: (50) They kindle and bless — although in synagogue only custom, nevertheless bless as one blesses on Rosh Chodesh Hallel which is only custom. If mourner leads prayers on Hanukkah eve, another kindles lights because of shehecheyanu blessed then — recognizable joy for congregation, unseemly mourner kindle them [at home he may bless shehecheyanu]. Other Hanukkah evenings without shehecheyanu — mourner may kindle Hanukkah light; mourner leads Minchah and Ma'ariv on Hanukkah; on 15 Av, Shabbat, Lag BaOmer without Hallel mourner also leads Shacharit; on chol ha'moed like Yom Tov I sometimes prevented mourner leading Minchah and Ma'ariv [Peri Megadim].
mishnah-berurah/7:פ: (80) Before Minchah — so Maharshal; Darkei Moshe wrote we do not practice thus, but even Shabbat eve kindle in synagogue between Minchah and Ma'ariv when people begin gathering — there is pirsumei nisa; however if people delay coming and day not sanctified until minyan in synagogue — do not wait, bless and kindle immediately even before Minchah, nevertheless pirsumei nisa when they come to synagogue and see lights; for individual see below end siman 679 Mishna Berurah.
mishnah-berurah/8:ה: (54) Inside literally — meaning in Tur's time they kindled at house entrance from inside and made at least recognition for passersby; therefore suspicion wherever recognition not proper for passersby; unlike now kindling literally inside and we do not care at all to make recognition for public domain — therefore we do not care for their suspicion.
peri-megadim/1:ב: The layman writer says: I have thoughts here and I set them forth with God's help. Rama chapter 4 halacha 3: simple custom in Spain, etc., Beit Yosef and Be'er HaGolah brought — one may explain as Lechem Mishneh there; one may strain and say they also do mehaderin from mehaderin; what he wrote whether many or one — meaning even if many, no recognition in many lights to distinguish, as Peri Chadash wrote; nevertheless plain meaning does not imply so; Mechaber in Shulchan Aruch wrote in explanation mehaderin from mehaderin kindle only one light for whole household, otherwise no recognition for miracle addition as Tosafot there; nevertheless called mehaderin more than those kindling per person because more hidur for Beit Shammai night one eight seven six, etc., informing miracle continued eight full days — great miracle; if each kindled per person, no recognition miracle eight days — passerby says so many people in house; for Beit Shammai night one no hidur even for Beit Hillel night three no recognition for one who did night two not night one; Peri Chadash explains per person — intent: they will say guests added or household members not relying on table law — each needs light by law only one per household suffices — see there. For Tosafot mehaderin per person even ten households — why not more hidur one light and add? — one could say they are not so precise and understand; however must know: by law one light suffices man and household — man, wife, servant, adult son at his table; mehaderin do, etc.; but two households and guest — each obligated separately or with partners; Eliyah Rabbah 3: wife as his body; likewise siman 677; Rashi each two d.h. household lights — mehaderin for household implies so, excluding wife need not mehaderin; Ra'avan regarding guest not included in man and wife — some say so; man and household implies wife, mehaderin, etc.; minors of chinuch included in mehaderin — clear siman 675 seif 3; difficult chinuch even rabbinic — nevertheless mehaderin not chinuch — see there and below from this; if he kindled one light and did not bless — perhaps should not bless again, for he needs performer for doing them, others how say "and commanded us" — only one light mitzvah, only mehaderin, etc.; also primary preferable other lights — only one light siman 678; but siman 676 and Magen Avraham Beit Yosef 672 if forgot, etc., kindle and not bless — implies if interrupted in speech he blesses — yet only one mitzvah light and forbidden to use all lights; Rama chapter 4 halacha 1 men and women — see there; Eliyah Rabbah 2 Shabbat light — difficult implies only rabbinic; oneg Shabbat itself also rabbinic — responsa Chacham Tzvi; and mehaderin per person means intending not to fulfill with friend's — Mechaber ruled anonymously implies addition by law — requires study, practical difference exists — see Magen Avraham I will explain further.
peri-megadim/2:ב: Layman writer in rabbi's Hagahah words: I saw to explain a little what he wrote; not in circle Darkei Moshe wrote as in synagogue they nail pegs — if meaning nail pegs in wall in circle or around one round board nail pegs in circle — howsoever some difference between candlestick and this — one could say; see Peri Chadash. See Mishna Berurah wrote each separated from fellow not called bonfire; here wrote much separated; Terumat HaDeshen 105 22 not like candlestick where each reed separated by partition; also Ba'al HaItur in bowl two fingers permitted, here far apart — see there. Mechaber forbids in bowl even far apart like Tur; Mishna Berurah silent concedes; except candlestick stringent: reeds must be separated and far more than two fingers — here lacking one: not separated by partitions or separated but reeds not two fingers apart — forbidden as bonfire. Therefore requires study when gluing wax candles to wall not two fingers apart — forbidden; Eliyah Rabbah Tur finger, Terumat HaDeshen two fingers — see Magen Avraham 4 will explain further.
peri-megadim/5:א: Above twenty Taz, likewise Bach; Tosafot Sukkah 2 d.h. v'kiyvan crossbeam of alley even on alley walls tefach not recognizable — likewise Hanukkah light; Avnei Nezer. Therefore Shabbat 22 Hanukkah light invalid above twenty amot like sukkah and like alley — what is alley: even walls reaching crossbeam invalid, likewise here; sukkah too for Rava halacha follows him — even reaching sechach invalid siman 633; Ateret Zekenim in name of Mahara of Prague. In synagogue place in window near public domain — Peri Chadash if height twenty no elevation at all; nevertheless for us kindling inside may place in window; nevertheless some recognition for public — preferable thus; see Magen Avraham 10 and 14 I will explain further.
rabbi-akiva-eiger/3:_: {Rama: Seif 7} Be'er HaGolah: although only custom. So in Rivash — similar to Rosh Chodesh Hallel — responsa Chacham Tzvi siman 87 questioned: Mechaber holds siman 422 no blessing on Rosh Chodesh Hallel — wrote not practiced in all Land of Israel and surroundings — how rule here like Rivash in Land of Israel where no Hallel blessing? Proper not to bless on synagogue kindling — see there.
rabbi-akiva-eiger/4:_: {Rama: Seif 4 in Hagahah} that each light much separated from its fellow. Two fingers and separated by partitions — Terumat HaDeshen; Maharshal siman 85 wrote: when far apart without covering vessel counts as one light not many lights.
shaarei-teshuvah/2:_: Adds and goes on, etc. Eliyah Rabbah in name of Knesset HaGedolah, etc., to kindle after Ma'ariv; Shevut Yaakov; afterward brought Magen Avraham and Knesset HaGedolah; examiner in Shevut Yaakov sees Eliyah Rabbah's words reversed — there brought Magen Avraham and wrote on this; however Knesset HaGedolah writes "and in my choice, etc., I returned to my custom to kindle after evening prayer" — such is essential law — certainly frequent comes first as one can do both as Tosafot Shabbat 23 — see there; see below end siman 672; see Yad Ephraim; see Eshel Avraham here Shav Yaakov; see Machatzit HaShekel room for four views Maharash conclusion siman 2; Machatzit HaShekel concluded one who kindles before going to pray Ma'ariv has not lost — concern until Ma'ariv time passes — half hour Gemara law — see there.
shaarei-teshuvah/8:_: Ten handbreadths. Eliyah Rabbah; see Peri Megadim wondered: Tur Choshen Mishpat siman 418 rules like Tana Kama R' Yehuda — how rule here like Rabbina aliba d'R' Yehuda? See there at length; Shevut Yaakov part 3 wrote dispute of rabbis means even in reshut obligated — thus R' Yehuda says Hanukkah exempt because in reshut; also how say this teaches, etc., not halacha — see there; see Tosefta chapter 6 Bava Kamma teaches R' Yehuda Hanukkah exempt because placed in reshut — between this and that obligated, such as those roofing shop entrances in public domain — even though they have reshut, another came injured — liable; see there language somewhat as Shevut Yaakov wrote — not because above camel and rider, but even if mitzvah to place within ten handbreadths and in reshut — nevertheless if injured, liable; see Machatzit HaShekel on this. Eliyah Rabbah brought Seder HaYom: mitzvah above ten until eighteen — menorah height eighteen; Eliyah Rabbah wondered on him — from where below ten not? Machatzit HaShekel: since Rif and Rambam omitted R' Yehoshua must place below, etc. — presumably Hanukkah law like sukkah and alley; so Rama in Alfasi Zuta — see there; Tur Berakhet wrote mitzvah slightly above seven handbreadths; end Shomer Emunim siman 5 wrote Ari has source — see there.
turei-zahav/7:ג: And they bless in synagogue. Rama wrote in responsa siman 43: if mourner prays Hanukkah eve, another kindles lights because of shehecheyanu; other Hanukkah evenings — mourner kindles and prays.
turei-zahav/8:ב: And no recognition for public domain, etc. Tur likewise in name of Ba'al HaTurei Zahav and wrote on this: it appears not to be lenient, for even for us there is concern since kindling at house entrance passersby see he did not kindle — suspicion — end; therefore Rama answered to resolve: nowadays kindle literally inside, etc., unlike Tur's difficulty in his time — they kindled at house entrance, made recognition for passersby as end siman 671 — therefore suspicion wherever recognition not proper for passersby; unlike now kindling literally inside and we do not care to make recognition for public — therefore we do not care for their suspicion.
yad-ephraim/1:_: In Taz s.k. 5 at end: light of candle above — eye does not dominate there — as should be.
yad-ephraim/4:_: In Magen Avraham s.k. 8: nevertheless custom, etc. — this applies to what Hagahah wrote: nevertheless custom to kindle in handbreadth, etc.; Darkei Moshe — so in long Darkei Moshe Florence edition Hagahah there; what wrote place in window — no danger concern — appears error, should read: nowadays no danger concern — abbreviation bazman hazeh; meaning above seif 5 place in window near public domain, in danger place on table — on this wrote bazman hazeh no danger unless common damage place fears kindling, etc.; also since kindling literally inside as Rama below seif 8: bazman hazeh, etc., no danger — requires study per explicit danger concern Taz s.k. 3.
